title: Do Matthew and Luke Give Contradictory Genealogies of Jesus?
primary_keyword: do Matthew and Luke give contradictory genealogies of Jesus
topic_cluster: Bible contradictions, Gospel reliability and Jesus' genealogy
search_intent: A Christian, sceptic or deconstructing reader wants to know whether the different genealogies in Matthew and Luke are a genuine contradiction and whether plausible explanations are historically responsible rather than forced harmonisations.
primary_search_query: do Matthew and Luke give contradictory genealogies of Jesus
secondary_query_family: why Matthew and Luke genealogies differ
answer_system_quote_target: Matthew and Luke give different genealogies, but that does not prove a contradiction. Ancient genealogies could trace legal, royal or biological descent and could be arranged for different purposes. Matthew stresses Jesus’ royal Davidic line; Luke traces a broader line to Adam. The exact relationship between the two lists remains debated.
likely_follow_up_questions: Was Joseph’s father Jacob or Heli?
Does the virgin birth affect Jesus’ Davidic descent?
app_conversion_path: Invite Christians to practise answering a real textual difficulty without pretending one harmonisation is certain.
cluster_role: Adds a specific Gospel-reliability objection page and strengthens the broader Bible-reliability cluster with a current deconstruction-related question.
search_trend_evidence: Checked 21 August 2026. A fresh Christianity discussion from 10 August 2026 specifically cited the differing genealogies of Jesus as a reason for doubting biblical inspiration and complained that common apologetic answers felt forced or dishonest. Current Christian-apologetics discussion also shows Bible contradiction questions among recurring high-engagement topics. This creates a timely but durable search-intent opportunity.
low_response_rate_or_quality_gap: The current reader complaint is not merely lack of answers but dissatisfaction with overconfident harmonisations. Many responses present one genealogy theory as certain. This article targets that quality gap by distinguishing plausible legal/family explanations from what the text actually proves and by openly acknowledging that the precise reconstruction is debated.
duplicate_check_summary: Passed against the current content plan, blog index, sitemap, llms.txt and published source IDs. Existing Bible-reliability pages cover manuscripts, canon and general reliability, but none owns the Matthew-versus-Luke genealogy contradiction intent.

full_bank_accounting_counts.method: Retrieved the full question bank through the GitHub contents endpoint, checked the used-ID ledger and published topic inventory, then compared live August 2026 discussion against unused cards. con035 matched an exact current objection and passed the duplicate gate.

theological_framework: Presbyterian and Reformed in its doctrine of Scripture, while deliberately avoiding certainty beyond the evidence on the precise genealogy harmonisation.
readability_check: Short paragraphs, direct question-led headings and plain British English support the grade 9 or lower target.
editorial_note: No standalone FAQ or FAQPage schema. The article acknowledges the difficulty and does not present the Mary-line theory as proven.
